module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 351

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/351](https://www.erdosproblems.com/351)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Polynomial

namespace Erdos351

/-- The set of rational numbers of the form `P(n) + 1 / n` where `n` is a natural number
and `P` is a polynomial with rational coefficients.

Note: We include `P 0` in there (since `1 / 0 = 0`), but this doesn't change the validity of the
conjecture -/
def imageSet {α : Type*} [Semifield α] (P : α[X]) : Set α :=
  Set.range (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ P.eval ↑n + 1 / n)

/-- The predicate that a set `A` is strongly complete, i.e. that for every finite set `B`, every sufficiently
large integer is a sum of elements of the set `A \ B`. -/
def IsStronglyComplete {α : Type*} [Semiring α] (A : Set α) : Prop :=
  ∀ B : Finset α,
    ∀ᶠ (m : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
      ↑m ∈ { ∑ n ∈ X, n | (X : Finset α) (_ : ↑X ⊆ A \ B) }

/-- The predicate that the rational polynomial `P` has a complete image. -/
def HasCompleteImage (P : ℚ[X]) : Prop := IsStronglyComplete (imageSet P)

/--
Let $p(x) \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$ be a non-constant rational polynomial with positive leading
coefficient. Is it true that $$A=\{ p(n)+1/n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$$ is strongly complete,
in the sense that, for any finite set $B$,
$$\left\{\sum_{a \in X} a : X \subseteq A \setminus B, X \textrm{ is finite}\right\}$$
contains all sufficiently large integers? -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos351.lean"]
theorem erdos_351 :
    answer(True) ↔ ∀ P : ℚ[X], 0 < P.natDegree → 0 < P.leadingCoeff → HasCompleteImage P := by
  sorry

/--
Let $p(x) = x \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$. It has been shown that
$$A=\{ p(n)+1/n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$$
is strongly complete, in the sense that, for any finite set $B$,
$$\left\{\sum_{a \in X} a : X \subseteq A \setminus B, X \textrm{ is finite}\right\}$$
contains all sufficiently large integers.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
protected theorem erdos_351.variants.X : HasCompleteImage X := by
  sorry

/-- Let $p(x) = x ^ 2 \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$. It has been shown that
$$A=\{ p(n)+1/n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$$
is strongly complete, in the sense that, for any finite set $B$,
$$\left\{\sum_{a \in X} a : X \subseteq A \setminus B, X \textrm{ is finite}\right\}$$
contains all sufficiently large integers. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_351.variants.X_sq : HasCompleteImage (X ^ 2) := by
  sorry

end Erdos351

reformulations.difference: The Lean statement adds the hypothesis `0 < P.natDegree` (non-constant). The source has no such condition: erdosproblems.com/351 reads "Let p(x) ∈ ℚ[x] with positive leading coefficient", so positive constants are included. The docstring also says "non-constant". The Lean is therefore weaker in form than the source.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The excluded case is true by an elementary argument, so the two statements are provably equivalent without touching the hard part of the problem. For a constant c = a/b > 0 the set is {c + 1/n}. Pick N beyond the finitely many n with c + 1/n ∈ B (n ↦ c + 1/n is injective). Every natural r is a sum of distinct unit fractions with all denominators > N: take a harmonic block (N, M], then run the Fibonacci–Sylvester greedy algorithm with a lower bound on the denominators. Replacing the largest denominator M by M+1 and M(M+1) adds one term and keeps the sum, so every size k ≥ |S_r| is reachable. Given m large, take r = a + (m mod a), j = m/a − 1 and k = b·j; then c·k + r = m. I proved this in Lean with no sorry and only the standard axioms (/workspace/review/equiv.lean). `Review.const_case : ∀ c : ℚ, 0 < c → Erdos351.HasCompleteImage (C c)`. `Review.source_iff_file : (∀ P, 0 < P.leadingCoeff → HasCompleteImage P) ↔ (∀ P, 0 < P.natDegree → 0 < P.leadingCoeff → HasCompleteImage P)`. `Review.faithful_iff_file` states the literal source form (strong completeness of {P(n)+1/n : n ≥ 1} for every P with positive leading coefficient) and proves it equivalent to the file's right-hand side. The linked external formal proof (plby/lean-proofs, `corollary_7_pos_leading`) also covers constants with identical definitions, and its comments note that FC separately requires `0 < natDegree`.

reformulations.difference: `imageSet P` is `Set.range (fun n : ℕ ↦ P.eval n + 1/n)`, so it includes n = 0. There, 1/0 = 0 contributes the extra element P(0). The source's A = {p(n)+1/n : n ∈ ℕ} uses n ≥ 1. This affects `erdos_351`, `erdos_351.variants.X` and `erdos_351.variants.X_sq`. The file's own docstring notes the convention.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Adding one element x does not change strong completeness. If A is strongly complete, so is A ∪ {x} (monotonicity). Conversely, apply strong completeness of A ∪ {x} with the finite set B ∪ {x}. Proved in Lean (/workspace/review/equiv.lean): `Review.isStronglyComplete_insert_iff`, `Review.imageSet_eq : imageSet P = insert (P.eval 0) (sourceSet P)`, and `Review.hasCompleteImage_iff : HasCompleteImage P ↔ IsStronglyComplete {P(n)+1/n : n ≥ 1}`. The docstring's claim that this "doesn't change the validity" is correct.

review.notes:
No findings. Every declaration states the claim the source (erdosproblems.com/351) currently poses, up to two harmless conventions. I proved both harmless in Lean with no sorry and only the standard axioms: /workspace/review/equiv.lean, `Review.faithful_iff_file`.

Checks done:
- `1 / n` elaborates as division in ℚ, not ℕ (checked with pp.all).
- `IsStronglyComplete` quantifies over every finite B and every sufficiently large natural m cast into ℚ. It sums over Finsets, i.e. distinct elements, which matches the source's "X ⊆ A \ B finite". It deliberately does not use the shared `IsAddStronglyComplete`: on ℚ that would demand all large rationals, which is the old wording the forum identified as wrong (Kovač; Bloom agreed "sufficiently large integers" is intended).
- `answer(True)` matches the source's "PROVED (LEAN) … solved in the affirmative", and the `research solved` tag is correct. The formal_proof link proves exactly this statement with identical definitions.
- `variants.X` (Graham [Gr63]; the forum confirms Graham's theorem gives all a_i ≥ m, hence strong completeness) and `variants.X_sq` (van Doorn, via [Gr63] + Alekseyev) match the source's remarks. Both are correctly tagged solved.

History: before Dec 2025 the source read "Let p(x) ∈ ℚ[x]" with no sign condition. AlphaProof disproved that with p(x) = −x (Dillies' forum comment). The FC file and then the site (10 May 2026) added the positive-leading-coefficient condition. "Non-constant" is FC's own addition. It is unnecessary but provably immaterial, so maintainers could drop `0 < P.natDegree` (and "non-constant" in the docstring) to match the source word for word; this is optional.

I could not read the original [ErGr80, p.58] text itself. The comparison relies on erdosproblems.com's statement, its history and its forum thread.
